# Evidence of capability: scoring accurately, observing less, and explaining predictions

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-13 · 22 topic entries / 14 representative comparisons

Distinguish how correctness is defined, which example to test next, how judges are combined, and what an explanation says. XLGoBench, ProEval, FUSE, TCAB, and DetectorScope change different parts. Fewer observations and additive explanations do not imply stronger underlying capability. XLA from the Trenches adds a prior concern: compiled execution can silently depart from numerical program semantics. Successful compilation does not establish correct execution.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### What do deterministic scoring and probabilistic surrogates answer?

XLGoBench computes exact algorithmic answers for structured outputs. ProEval keeps task correctness fixed and predicts overall performance from observed scores. Posterior means and variances come from model relationships, not real scoring of every question. Combine the ideas by isolating scorer gold, then deciding which legitimate scores to pay for while separating inferred and observed outcomes.

Sources: [XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks](../../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en.md) · [ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en.md)

### An extra layer of evidence is not automatically reliable

FUSE uses multiple verifiers without true labels, but correlations and identification assumptions govern its posterior. DetectorScope decomposes logits exactly but shows only numerical contributions of pooled features, not truthful concepts or causal text effects. TCAB constrains marginal distributions under feedback reuse. These checks address different issues, and neither fluent explanations nor reuse rates verify capability.

Sources: [FUSE: Ensembling Verifiers with Zero Labeled Data](../../../../foundation-models/2604.18547-fuse-verifiers/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md) · [Fast A/B/n Testing: Exact Multi-Policy Comparison via Tree-Coupled Feedback Sharing](../../../../reproductions/2608.12831-tcab/README-en.md)

### The reference must match execution semantics too

XLGoBench separates scorers from gold. XLA shows that even valid tasks and labels do not guarantee compiled computation preserves program semantics: register rounding or fusion scheduling can change results. Differential references must exclude NaN-producing invalid inputs without flagging legitimate TPU approximations as bugs. A correct split fusion does not validate the intact fusion, and correct A100 computation does not validate TPU lowering. This batch preserves the missing TPU environment instead of replacing hardware conclusions with CPU/CUDA demonstrations.

Sources: [XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks](../../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en.md) · [XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale](../../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en.md)

### Rosetta: representation unification and cross-language transfer: intervention and evidence are different axes

Rosetta studies pretraining language distributions and representation unification; Thinking to Recall analyzes generated reasoning facts and their correctness. Similarity is not a truth judge, and oracle-conditioned accuracy does not establish multilingual unification. The two functions implement finite nonzero set-cosine arithmetic and per-group ratios, rejecting unstable denominators. Negative controls check scale invariance and mean-of-ratios behavior. Representations are external inputs, so these checks provide no evidence of improved multilingual capability.

Sources: [Beyond the Rosetta Stone: Unification Forces in Generalization Dynamics](../../../../foundation-models/2508.11017-rosetta-unification/README-en.md) · [Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2603.09906-thinking-to-recall/README-en.md)

### Thinking to Recall: offline conditional accuracy of factual traces: intervention and evidence are different axes

Not by this component. It uses post-hoc truth annotations to estimate offline conditional expectations. Deployment needs an oracle-free verifier with measured errors and costs. The interface returns aggregate rates and retention counts only—not selected traces, actions or training examples—and defaults to exactly 100 samples per question. `pass_at_k` uses the combinatorial unbiased estimator. Controls cover the common question mask, macro rather than micro averaging, empty facts and missing subsets. Synthetic truth arrays are explicit evaluator fixtures, not agent scores.

Sources: [Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2603.09906-thinking-to-recall/README-en.md) · [Beyond the Rosetta Stone: Unification Forces in Generalization Dynamics](../../../../foundation-models/2508.11017-rosetta-unification/README-en.md)

### Latent generalization: separating exposed and held-out answer-set recall: intervention and evidence are different axes

Latent generalization uses controlled acquisition/structure splits to test implicit completions; Thinking to Recall studies access to existing factual knowledge. Neither permits gold-conditioned teachers or post-hoc truth labels to leak to the deployed actor. Input checks require a nonempty held-out subset and a held-out primary. Exact-set pass@N is estimated from completed independent attempts. Negative controls show that perfect exposed recall can coexist with zero held-out recall, and perfect held-out recall can still fail exact matching through false additions. This is CPU offline evaluation, without model training, semantic judging or Evolve promotion.

Sources: [Improving Latent Generalization Using Test-time Compute](../../../../foundation-models/2604.01430-latent-generalization/README-en.md) · [Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2603.09906-thinking-to-recall/README-en.md)

### A goodness-of-fit p-value is not event mass under a decoding distribution

LLM Stochasticity checks finite samples against target marginals and uses temporal statistics to expose cycles or dependence. Non-rejection establishes neither the null distribution nor independence. Decoding-constrained beam search fixes per-step top-k normalization, never renormalizes survivors after distance pruning, and sums feasible complete-path mass into a lower bound while retaining possible pruned mass in a bank. This is an event-mass bound, not a goodness-of-fit p-value. A combined evaluation must report sampling protocols and risk events separately: p=1 is neither 100% randomness nor 100% extraction probability. Both local components validate numerical/protocol properties without loading an LLM for a complete audit.

Sources: [The Illusion of Stochasticity in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2604.06543-llm-stochasticity/README-en.md) · [Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search](../../../../foundation-models/2603.24917-decoding-constrained-beam/README-en.md)

### Changing supervision units differs from subtracting an inference baseline

QE normalization changes training labels so the model predicts error per unit length before restoring ratings. Interpolated Null Calibration retains a trained model and subtracts a nuisance baseline using query-plus-instruction, instruction-inclusive null and bare-null readouts. Frozen-score division cannot replace the former; lambda0 in the latter still subtracts bare null. Both require explicit controlled factors and validation selection, but model stages, observations and error sources differ. Correct arithmetic establishes neither unexecuted QE retraining nor missing model readouts.

Sources: [Penalizing Length: Uncovering Systematic Bias in Quality Estimation Metrics](../../../../foundation-models/2510.22028-qe-length-normalization/README-en.md) · [How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking](../../../../foundation-models/2609.17764-interpolated-null-calibration/README-en.md)

### A sparse representation can support detection or intervention without making their evidence interchangeable

Both methods pool SAE activations but require different evidence. CuE builds directions from cultural information and prototypes; DetectorScope validates feature descriptions and fits a sparse detector. A real intervention needs decoder alignment and generation evaluation, whereas detector contributions explain its logit. Shared pooling cannot turn correlation into cultural control or a synthetic direction norm into faithfulness.

Sources: [Steering LLMs for Culturally Localized Generation](../../../../foundation-models/2603.23301-cultural-cue/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)

### Generatability, near-target probability and text authorship are different statistical questions

CBS bounds generation of a target neighborhood from a prefix; DetectorScope predicts source from text features. A common sentence can be highly generatable and independently human-written, while a detector score gives no extraction probability. Enumerated mass supplies a lower bound, and beam/distance settings alter recovered mass without turning unseen paths into successes. Distributional assumptions and negative controls cannot be replaced by a greedy hit rate.

Sources: [Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search](../../../../foundation-models/2603.24917-decoding-constrained-beam/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)

### Explanation granularity and dependence structure follow the source of features

StoryScope interprets narrative structures, whereas DetectorScope interprets internal sparse activations and descriptions. Both retain extraction costs and model errors. StoryScope must group six stories sharing a prompt and limit cross-model spread before calling a signal a general AI core. Sparse detector contributions explain a head, not an entire story's semantic construction. Each method needs its own inputs and evidence rather than a generic feature fixture.

Sources: [StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction](../../../../foundation-models/2604.03136-storyscope/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why must sparse ProEval testing still isolate real scorers and gold answers as XLGoBench does? {#cross-oracle-versus-surrogate}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** ProEval changes measurement selection and total-score estimation; observations still need legitimate task scoring. Leaking answers to the model or unqueried scores to the posterior contaminates results. Keep predictions, revealed scores, and scorer-internal gold separate.

    **Illustrative example:** Query item two before reading its score. Initializing with all target scores defeats a small-query evaluation.

    Sources: [ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en.md) · [XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks](../../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en.md)

### Why are FUSE correctness posteriors and DetectorScope concept contributions not direct truth proofs? {#cross-posterior-versus-explanation}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** FUSE estimates correctness under verifier behavior assumptions and can inherit correlated errors. DetectorScope measures the logit change when a pooled feature is zeroed, not whether a concept story is true or causally supported by text. Validate statistical reliability and explanations independently.

    **Illustrative example:** Judges that all prefer long answers can share a mistake, and a strong detector feature may reflect a dataset shortcut.

    Sources: [FUSE: Ensembling Verifiers with Zero Labeled Data](../../../../foundation-models/2604.18547-fuse-verifiers/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)

### Why not record TCAB shared feedback and ProEval imputed scores as the same observations? {#cross-shared-feedback-versus-imputed-feedback}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** TCAB reuses real feedback only on valid coupled identical decisions while preserving each policy's marginal process. ProEval predicts unqueried scores using historical covariance. Neither licenses reporting a different action's outcome or an untested score as executed.

    **Illustrative example:** Two policies choosing action A can share A's feedback. If another chooses B, its correlated history does not authorize assigning A's success to B.

    Sources: [Fast A/B/n Testing: Exact Multi-Policy Comparison via Tree-Coupled Feedback Sharing](../../../../reproductions/2608.12831-tcab/README-en.md) · [ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en.md)

### With exact XLGoBench gold, why doesn't completing a program guarantee trustworthy model evaluation? {#cross-nov04-labels-versus-execution-semantics}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Exact gold defines correct output, not whether compiled model execution preserves semantics. XLA demonstrates silent numerical changes without crashes. Valid inputs, hardware-matched differential references and isolation are still needed. Check label correctness separately from execution correctness to distinguish model errors from backend errors.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Gold requires a nonzero quantization residual, but a TPU fused kernel outputs zeros after skipping casts. An exact scorer can mark the output wrong; it cannot automatically conclude the model lacks the ability.

    Sources: [XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks](../../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en.md) · [XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale](../../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en.md)

### How does Rosetta differ from Thinking to Recall? {#cross-nov13-colm-rosetta-unification}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Rosetta studies pretraining language distributions and representation unification; Thinking to Recall analyzes generated reasoning facts and their correctness. Similarity is not a truth judge, and oracle-conditioned accuracy does not establish multilingual unification.

    **Illustrative example:** More similar language representations do not verify a generated birthday; verified reasoning facts do not ensure low-resource-language access.

    Sources: [Beyond the Rosetta Stone: Unification Forces in Generalization Dynamics](../../../../foundation-models/2508.11017-rosetta-unification/README-en.md) · [Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2603.09906-thinking-to-recall/README-en.md)

### Can the clean-fact condition be deployed as an agent policy? {#cross-nov13-colm-thinking-to-recall}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not by this component. It uses post-hoc truth annotations to estimate offline conditional expectations. Deployment needs an oracle-free verifier with measured errors and costs.

    **Illustrative example:** Choosing a trace by gold correctness and feeding it to an actor leaks the answer rather than improving reasoning.

    Sources: [Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2603.09906-thinking-to-recall/README-en.md) · [Beyond the Rosetta Stone: Unification Forces in Generalization Dynamics](../../../../foundation-models/2508.11017-rosetta-unification/README-en.md)

### What differs from Thinking to Recall? {#cross-nov13-colm-latent-generalization}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Latent generalization uses controlled acquisition/structure splits to test implicit completions; Thinking to Recall studies access to existing factual knowledge. Neither permits gold-conditioned teachers or post-hoc truth labels to leak to the deployed actor.

    **Illustrative example:** Better recall of one fact does not establish generalization to an unseen reversal relation.

    Sources: [Improving Latent Generalization Using Test-time Compute](../../../../foundation-models/2604.01430-latent-generalization/README-en.md) · [Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2603.09906-thinking-to-recall/README-en.md)

### Can a uniform cycle's chi-square p-value of one be compared directly with a decoding-constrained extraction-risk lower bound of 0.1? {#cross-nov13-colm-llm-stochasticity}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The p-value reflects non-rejection of a marginal-frequency test; a deterministic cycle can still be fully predictable. It is not an output-event probability. The lower bound is enumerated path mass for a specified top-k decoding distribution and target-distance event. Objects, assumptions and denominators differ, and neither value establishes temporal independence.

    **Illustrative example:** A repeating 0,1,2,3 sequence can have a perfect 1,024-sample histogram while its next symbol is determined by the previous one. A separate model's probability tree may assign at least 0.1 mass to an enumerated target neighborhood, without establishing whether sampling uses an independent random source.

    Sources: [The Illusion of Stochasticity in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2604.06543-llm-stochasticity/README-en.md) · [Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search](../../../../foundation-models/2603.24917-decoding-constrained-beam/README-en.md)

### Can three-pass null-score subtraction replace error-density training merely because both are called calibration? {#cross-cross-density-versus-temperature}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Density training changes supervision to R/|h| and restores the length scale later. Null calibration subtracts an interpolated baseline from existing readouts. Neither executes the other's model stage, and tunable choices must use validation.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: scores0.8,0.3,0.1 with lambda0.5 yield calibrated score0.6. This is not the density target−0.5 for rating−5 and length10.

    Sources: [Penalizing Length: Uncovering Systematic Bias in Quality Estimation Metrics](../../../../foundation-models/2510.22028-qe-length-normalization/README-en.md) · [How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking](../../../../foundation-models/2609.17764-interpolated-null-calibration/README-en.md)

### Why are CuE and DetectorScope different despite both max-pooling SAE features? {#cross-cross-cue-versus-detectorscope}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Pooling is only a shared representation step. CuE selects feature-country information and constructs residual interventions from prototype differences. DetectorScope uses description-validation masks and a sparse detection head with attributions. A steering direction is not a detector and a head weight is not a cultural intervention.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a food feature may distinguish countries without distinguishing human from AI text. A large detection contribution does not establish culturally faithful generation when steering it.

    Sources: [Steering LLMs for Culturally Localized Generation](../../../../foundation-models/2603.23301-cultural-cue/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)

### Can a CBS probability lower bound replace a DetectorScope AI-authorship score? {#cross-cross-logprob-bound-versus-detector}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. CBS uses a target suffix and model conditionals to bound near-target generation mass. DetectorScope predicts source from SAE text features. High generatability is not proof of authorship, and the statistics have different targets and labels.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a common public sentence may have high model probability while being human-written. An authorship score likewise does not establish extraction probability for a training passage.

    Sources: [Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search](../../../../foundation-models/2603.24917-decoding-constrained-beam/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)

### Where do StoryScope and DetectorScope obtain interpretability, and are their features interchangeable? {#cross-cross-storyscope-versus-detectorscope}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** StoryScope uses externally assigned semantic narrative questions with classifier/SHAP analysis. DetectorScope uses internal SAE features and an additive sparse head. Their explanation units, costs and errors differ; random SAE columns cannot replace uncomputed narrative assignments.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: deciding whether an ending states its theme requires semantic reading. The contribution of a numbered SAE column is a separate observation.

    Sources: [StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction](../../../../foundation-models/2604.03136-storyscope/README-en.md) · [Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en.md)
